/-!
# Conjecture 2.24

by A. I. Kokorin

Are Engel torsion-free groups orderable?

Here an Engel group is a group in which every element is an Engel element, that
is, for all $x, y \in G$ there is some $n = n(x, y)$ with $[x,\, {}_n y] = 1$;
the length $n$ may depend on the pair $x, y$. We reuse the definition
`Kourovka.«1.40».IsEngelGroup`. A group is torsion-free if its only element of
finite order is the identity. In Kokorin's terminology a group is orderable if
it admits a linear order that is invariant under multiplication on both sides.
Every orderable group is torsion-free, which motivates the hypothesis.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.code:
@[category research open, AMS 6 20]
theorem kourovka.«2.24» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Kourovka.«1.40».IsEngelGroup G →
      (∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1) →
      ∃ _ : LinearOrder G, MulLeftMono G ∧ MulRightMono G := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
Are Engel torsion-free groups orderable?

That is, does every torsion-free Engel group $G$ admit a linear order $\le$
such that $a \le b$ implies $ca \le cb$ and $ac \le bc$ for all $a, b, c \in G$?

Torsion-freeness is stated as: every element of finite order is the identity.
For non-commutative groups this is weaker than `IsMulTorsionFree`, which asserts
uniqueness of roots.

@[category research open, AMS 6 20]
theorem kourovka.«2.24» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Kourovka.«1.40».IsEngelGroup G →

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question, implicitly quantified over all groups G: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ G, (G Engel, i.e. every element is an Engel element with the Engel length n depending on the pair of elements, not bounded n-Engel — cf. IsEngelGroup in Kourovka/1_40.lean) ∧ G torsion-free → G is orderable; 'orderable' in Kokorin's terminology means bi-orderable (a linear order on G invariant under both left and right multiplication, e.g. ∃ LinearOrder G with IsOrderedMonoid G / MulLeftMono ∧ MulRightMono), not merely right-orderable, and torsion-freeness is the necessary condition motivating the hypothesis.
claims.reviewer_why: c04 is the only candidate that both reuses the existing `Kourovka.«1.40».IsEngelGroup` (unbounded, pair-dependent Engel length; repo precedent for importing another problem file exists, e.g. Wikipedia/HadwigerNelson imports ErdosProblems.«508») and renders torsion-freeness faithfully as `∀ g, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1`. Edits: added the required `import FormalConjecturesUtil` (the import linter is enabled in CI and c04 omitted it), wrote the conclusion as `∃ _ : LinearOrder G, MulLeftMono G ∧ MulRightMono G` (same content, form used by c06/c07/c08), AMS tags `6 20`, and docstrings adapted from c06/c08. c01, c02, c03, c05 were rejected because they use Mathlib's `IsMulTorsionFree`, which is defined as injectivity of all power maps a ↦ a^n (unique roots / R-group property); for non-commutative groups this is strictly stronger than torsion-free (Klein bottle group: torsion-free but (ab)^2 = a^2 with ab ≠ a), and Mathlib proves the equivalence only for `CommGroup`. Since bi-orderable groups have unique roots and it is not known that torsion-free Engel groups do, this changes the question. c06/c07/c08 are faithful but duplicate the 1_40 definitions instead of reusing them; c04's reuse is preferred by AGENTS.md ('search nearby problem files before you add a definition').

/-!
# Conjecture 2.24

by A. I. Kokorin

Are Engel torsion-free groups orderable?

Here an Engel group is a group in which every element is an Engel element, that
is, for all $x, y \in G$ there is some $n = n(x, y)$ with $[x,\, {}_n y] = 1$;
the length $n$ may depend on the pair $x, y$. We reuse the definition
`Kourovka.«1.40».IsEngelGroup`. A group is torsion-free if its only element of
finite order is the identity. In Kokorin's terminology a group is orderable if
it admits a linear order that is invariant under multiplication on both sides.
Every orderable group is torsion-free, which motivates the hypothesis.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«2.24»

/--
Are Engel torsion-free groups orderable?

That is, does every torsion-free Engel group $G$ admit a linear order $\le$
such that $a \le b$ implies $ca \le cb$ and $ac \le bc$ for all $a, b, c \in G$?

Torsion-freeness is stated as: every element of finite order is the identity.
For non-commutative groups this is weaker than `IsMulTorsionFree`, which asserts
uniqueness of roots.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 6 20]
theorem kourovka.«2.24» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Kourovka.«1.40».IsEngelGroup G →
      (∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1) →
      ∃ _ : LinearOrder G, MulLeftMono G ∧ MulRightMono G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«2.24»

items: Reused `Kourovka.«1.40».IsEngelGroup`, which quantifies an Engel length separately for each pair of group elements and does not impose a uniform Engel bound.

Expressed ordinary group-theoretic torsion-freeness as `∀ g, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1`. Mathlib's `IsMulTorsionFree` was deliberately not used because for noncommutative groups it requires injectivity of all nonzero power maps, a stronger unique-roots condition.

Expressed bi-orderability by the existence of one `LinearOrder G` supporting both `MulLeftMono G` and `MulRightMono G`. Mathlib's `IsOrderedMonoid` was not used because its current definition requires a commutative monoid.

reviewer_notes: Statement is a single yes/no question: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsEngelGroup G → (∀ g, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1) → ∃ bi-invariant LinearOrder on G. Modeling notes: (1) 'orderable' read as bi-orderable (Kokorin/Kopytov 'O-group'), per the decomposition notes and the Russian-school terminology; `IsOrderedMonoid` cannot be used since it needs `CommMonoid`, so `MulLeftMono ∧ MulRightMono` over an existentially chosen `LinearOrder` is used (≤- vs <-invariance coincide in a group). (2) The Engel definition in 1_40 uses Mathlib's commutator ⁅a,b⁆ = aba⁻¹b⁻¹ while the notebook uses a⁻¹b⁻¹ab; one checks ⁅x,ₙy⁆ = yⁿ([x⁻¹,ₙy]_K)⁻¹y⁻ⁿ, so with ∀x∀y∃n quantification the group-level notion is identical. (3) Quantifying over `G : Type` follows the other Kourovka files; it is harmless because bi-orderability is a local property (a counterexample would have a finitely generated, hence countable, subgroup counterexample), and Engel/torsion-free pass to subgroups. (4) Reusing the definition by importing `FormalConjectures.Kourovka.«1_40»` follows existing precedent; a maintainer may prefer to move the Engel definitions into FormalConjecturesForMathlib and share them between 1_40 and 2_24. (5) Candidates also flagged that Wikipedia/Kaplansky.lean uses `IsMulTorsionFree` for 'torsion-free group', which may be worth a separate review. Final file built with `lake --wfail build` under the repo's CI lint options with no warnings.
